final_candidates.decision_summary: Removes the conserved negative charge at D473, which is expected to disrupt organic cation recognition/translocation. Chosen over D473N because it shows comparatively better evolutionary tolerance despite folding risk.

Isosteric charge neutralization of D473 should strongly impair cation transport while better preserving local geometry than alanine. Confidence is tempered by poor sequence-plausibility/tolerance signals and possible abundance effects.

Neutralizes a conserved basic residue in a functionally important intracellular/cavity region and is relatively better tolerated. It is ranked third because the available damaging/LOF-proxy signal is weaker than for D473 substitutions.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 ordering is unlikely to change without direct transport/abundance assays.

history.rationale: Aspartate at start of TM10/11-adjacent region (CDIGGI motif); neutralization may impair cation handling; Ala is small and tolerated.
Asp in TM11 region (TIDRVGRI motif) is highly conserved in OCTs and implicated in cation substrate recognition; neutralization should abolish transport while a small Ala preserves helix packing.

D473A has the strongest LOF-proxy signal and remains the only D473 variant with observed evolutionary tolerance, favoring transport loss without maximal folding risk. Its very low ESM plausibility tempers confidence.
Conserved basic residue in the large intracellular loop/adjacent TM region may influence gating of transport; Ala is structurally mild.
Basic residue within TM7-adjacent region likely contributes to the substrate translocation pathway; Ala substitution removes a charged interaction without large steric disruption.
R345A is comparatively better tolerated by MSA/PLM but has the weakest damaging/LOF-proxy signal, making it less likely to fully abolish transport.
Isosteric neutralization of the same conserved Asp removes the negative charge essential for organic cation transport while better preserving side-chain geometry and folding than Ala.
Isosteric Asp neutralization is mechanistically attractive for abolishing cation transport, but absent Asn at homologs and near-zero sequence plausibility raise abundance/folding concern.
